examples.title: Pets that follow the player
examples.prompt: Make a pet system where pets smoothly follow the player.
examples.code:
-- PetFollow (ModuleScript in ServerScriptService)
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local PetFollow = {}

-- Makes `pet` (a Model) follow `character` at `offset`, smoothly.
-- Returns the connection: call :Disconnect() when the pet is removed.
function PetFollow.follow(pet: Model, character: Model, offset: CFrame): RBXScriptConnection
	local root = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart") :: BasePart
	return RunService.Heartbeat:Connect(function(dt)
		if not pet.Parent or not root.Parent then
			return
		end
		local goal = root.CFrame * offset
		local alpha = math.min(dt * 8, 1)
		pet:PivotTo(pet:GetPivot():Lerp(goal, alpha))
	end)
end

return PetFollow
why: Lerp scaled by dt: same speed whatever the FPS
PivotTo moves the whole Model, not a single Part
Returns the connection so it can be disconnected (no leaks)
Small reusable function inside a ModuleScript

examples.title: Saving player data with DataStore
examples.prompt: Save the player's coins without ever losing data.
examples.code:
-- PlayerData (Script in ServerScriptService)
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")

local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerData_v1")
local DEFAULT = { Coins = 0 }

local function load(player: Player)
	local ok, data = pcall(function()
		return store:GetAsync("u_" .. player.UserId)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("Load failed for", player.Name, data)
		player:Kick("Your data could not be loaded, please rejoin.")
		return
	end
	data = data or table.clone(DEFAULT)

	local leaderstats = Instance.new("Folder")
	leaderstats.Name = "leaderstats"
	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
	coins.Name = "Coins"
	coins.Value = data.Coins
	coins.Parent = leaderstats
	leaderstats.Parent = player
end

local function save(player: Player)
	local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if not stats then
		return -- never overwrite saved data with empty data
	end
	local coins = stats.Coins.Value
	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		store:UpdateAsync("u_" .. player.UserId, function(old)
			old = old or table.clone(DEFAULT)
			old.Coins = coins
			return old
		end)
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("Save failed for", player.Name, err)
	end
end

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(load)
Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(save)
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
	task.spawn(load, player)
end

game:BindToClose(function()
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		task.spawn(save, player)
	end
	task.wait(3)
end)
why: Every DataStore call is wrapped in pcall
If loading fails the player is kicked, so empty data can never overwrite a real save
UpdateAsync instead of SetAsync: safe against concurrent writes
BindToClose saves everyone when the server shuts down

examples.title: Shop opening with a tween
examples.prompt: Animate my shop opening like in simulator games.
examples.code:
-- ShopToggle (LocalScript inside the shop button)
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local button = script.Parent
local shop = button.Parent:WaitForChild("ShopFrame")

local scale = shop:FindFirstChildOfClass("UIScale")
if not scale then
	scale = Instance.new("UIScale")
	scale.Parent = shop
end

local OPEN = TweenInfo.new(0.35, Enum.EasingStyle.Back, Enum.EasingDirection.Out)
local CLOSE = TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.In)

local isOpen = false
scale.Scale = 0
shop.Visible = false

button.Activated:Connect(function()
	isOpen = not isOpen
	if isOpen then
		shop.Visible = true
		TweenService:Create(scale, OPEN, { Scale = 1 }):Play()
	else
		local tween = TweenService:Create(scale, CLOSE, { Scale = 0 })
		tween.Completed:Once(function()
			if not isOpen then
				shop.Visible = false
			end
		end)
		tween:Play()
	end
end)
why: Tweening a UIScale keeps the layout intact (no Size/Position math)
Back easing gives the simulator-style pop
Activated works with mouse, touch and gamepad
Checks isOpen after the close tween, so a quick re-open is not hidden
examples.sources: Creator Docs: UI animation / tweens, UIScale

examples.title: Sword slash with a Beam and particles
examples.prompt: Add a slash effect when the player attacks.
examples.code:
-- SlashVFX (ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage)
-- Child template "Slash": a Part with a Beam and a ParticleEmitter named "Sparks".
local Debris = game:GetService("Debris")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local template = script:WaitForChild("Slash")

local SlashVFX = {}

function SlashVFX.play(origin: CFrame)
	local slash = template:Clone()
	slash.Anchored = true
	slash.CanCollide = false
	slash.CanQuery = false
	slash.Transparency = 1
	slash.CFrame = origin
	slash.Parent = workspace

	slash.Sparks:Emit(20)
	local sweep = origin * CFrame.Angles(0, math.rad(-120), 0)
	TweenService:Create(slash, TweenInfo.new(0.2, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad), { CFrame = sweep }):Play()

	local beam = slash:FindFirstChildOfClass("Beam")
	if beam then
		task.delay(0.15, function()
			beam.Enabled = false
		end)
	end
	Debris:AddItem(slash, 1)
end

return SlashVFX
why: Emit() gives one burst of particles instead of a constant stream
Debris cleans the effect up automatically
To check: play it on every client through a RemoteEvent so the server does not lag

examples.title: R6 idle played on the Animator
examples.prompt: Play my R6 idle animation when the character spawns.
examples.code:
-- IdleAnimation (LocalScript in StarterCharacterScripts)
local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")

local idle = Instance.new("Animation")
idle.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://0" -- replace with your animation ID

local track = animator:LoadAnimation(idle)
track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Idle
track.Looped = true
track:Play()
why: Idle priority so walking and attacks play on top
Draft: replacing the idle inside the default Animate script would be cleaner
